rationale: An exploratory state-anxiety comparison favored dried mixed berries versus cocoa in healthy volunteers. Raspberries constituted only 16.7% of the mixture, and the authors' test statistic and p-value need clarification. The whole frozen red-raspberry thesis measured oxidative biomarkers rather than anxiety, and raspberry powder studies do not disclose a separate controlled anxiety estimate in Parkinson disease. This evidence leaves the direction for frozen raspberry unresolved.

Fresh green kiwi gave an imprecise comparison on self-rated waking alertness. The registered breakfast trial found inconclusive choice reaction time and Stroop results in healthy adults using previously frozen pulp. The complete KINGS thesis reports overall fatigue and mood measures without a distinct attention outcome. The separate freeze-dried kiwi COMPASS registry has no posted results. The existing comparisons leave the direction for raw kiwi and Parkinson attention impairment unresolved.
